body:
Fixes #2571

Telegram API calls are now **governed**, not just counted. A big queue in one group no longer triggers bursts of 429s, and `/limits` stops reporting "19% used" right after a refusal. The production log ([case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2571-e18a3c59511b/docs/case-studies/issue-2571/README.md)) was used as a checklist. Every error and warning class in it is either fixed or now logs its reason.

## What changed

| Finding in the production log | Root cause | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 86 Telegram 429s, with `/limits` showing "observed limit 21, peak 23" and 19% used | The tracker only counted. Bursts that Telegram tolerated raised the learned limit, and refusals didn't slow anything down | Governor in `telegram-rate-limit.lib.mjs`: per-chat/group `retry_after` holds, pacing to the documented 1/s, 20/min and 30/s windows, refusals outranking successes for 30 min, and priorities (low = 75% of a window, never retried; normal = waits up to 75 s, retried once). Decisions are recorded synchronously. | `tests/telegram-rate-limit-governor.test.mjs` |
| 20+ waiting cards edited every cycle; 38% of edits re-sent identical text | Reasons carry CPU %, process counts and countdowns | Skip identical text. Edit at once only for a new reason kind or position; changes in numbers alone wait for the 5-min refresh. Card edits are low priority, and a chat stops being edited for the cycle after one refusal. | `tests/issue-2571-queue-telegram-edits.test.mjs` |
| Six `bot.catch` cascades of three 429s each | Error replies went into the chat that had just been throttled | No error reply into a rate-limited chat. `/top` and `/merge` refreshes are low priority and skip unchanged text. | `tests/telegram-rate-limit-governor.test.mjs` |
| `Can't find end of the entity` on the /stop "Cancelled" card | `@anton_poroshin` was not escaped for legacy Markdown | `escapeMarkdown` the user name and URL | `tests/issue-2571-cancel-card-markdown.test.mjs` |
| 131 Claude usage-API 429s and 564 Codex plus 43 Claude 401s | The 429 cache matched the wrong message text, and 401s were never cached | Failures classified as `auth` or `rate_limited`. A 429 is cached for max(TTL, `Retry-After`); an auth failure until the TTL ends or the credentials file changes. Concurrent callers share one in-flight request. Code moved to `usage-limits-cache.lib.mjs`. | `tests/issue-2571-usage-limits-cache.test.mjs` |
| `Failed to post comment with log link: unexpected end of JSON input` | GitHub's reply was cut off, so the comment may or may not exist | Look for the comment created since the request started. Reuse it if found, otherwise POST once more. | `tests/issue-2571-truncated-comment-response.test.mjs` |
| `agentic-cli-updater: 0 updated, 11 current, 2 failed` with no reason | The post-install version check and the unreachable-registry branch didn't log | Both log their reason, and the verbose summary lists `id: reason` | `tests/issue-2571-agentic-cli-update-failure-reason.test.mjs` |

`/limits` now also shows `Last 429: sendMessage, 1s ago, retry_after 8s`. When the bot restrained itself, it adds `Held back by the bot: 2 delayed, 50 skipped, 1 retried`. Both lines are translated in en, ru, zh and hi.

## Maintenance needed for CI

The dependency-freshness check needed lino-i18n ^0.3.0 and lino-objects-codec ^0.9.0. This branch also bumped start-command 0.35.4, command-stream 1.6.2, links-notation 0.23.0 and shell-quote (an audit advisory); main now has those too (#2499), so after merging main only the two lino bumps remain in this diff.

## Best practices checked

The Telegram Bots FAQ limits; grammY's flood-limit guide, auto-retry and transformer-throttler; telegraf-throttler; and python-telegram-bot's AIORateLimiter. The case study has a comparison table.

The design follows grammY's guidance: `retry_after` is authoritative, bursts are not parallelized, and low-value updates are dropped rather than queued. Unlike AIORateLimiter, it holds only the refused chat or group, not the whole bot.

## Upstream

No upstream issue was filed. The `gh` truncated-JSON response and the possible bun global-install mismatch each have only one occurrence and no reproducible example. The new logging collects the data an upstream report would need (see the case study).

## How to reproduce and verify

```
node tests/telegram-rate-limit-governor.test.mjs
node --test tests/issue-2571-*.test.mjs
node experiments/issue-2571-429-sequence.mjs path/to/hive-telegram-bot.log   # rebuilds the 429 sequence from a log
```

Every one of these tests fails on `main` and passes on this branch. The agentic-cli updater, cancel-card and truncated-comment tests fail on assertions that reproduce the logged bug. The governor, queue-edit and usage-cache tests fail on `main` sooner, because they import exports this PR adds (`LIMIT_EVIDENCE_TTL_MS`, `createTelegramLocalThrottleError`, `parseRetryAfterMs`).

title: Govern Telegram API calls after 429s, edit queue cards only for news, and fix production-log errors (#2571)
